name: Tony Medina
_presentation_note: PROMOTED 2026-09-06 on Daniel's call, reversing the 2026-08-16 spec'ing for this artist only. He was anonymous depth behind the 'Blues Rock' format because the workbook read him and Freddy Alexander as interchangeable. That reading does not survive contact with his own material: he fronts under his own name, on his own site and his own channel, with a published catalogue of originals and a covers book you can watch him play. That is the definition of a fronted act in _players_note, so he is named and the format he stood behind retires into him. Freddy stays below as unpublished depth, which is what the face-led promise already covers.
_status_note: A listing that owns a page, the same shape as the DJ. Not flagship: FLAGSHIPS drives the home page's three-up grid, and a fourth card would leave one orphan on a second row. He still gets the authored page, the 'See Tony Medina' card CTA and his own llms.txt URL, because both of those key off `page` rather than off status.
_style_note: Kept from the format he replaces. The card renders style as an eyebrow directly above the name, and 'Blues, rock and roots' over 'Tony Medina' reads as a byline rather than as the same two words twice.
_bucket_note: budget carries over from the format he replaces, and he is the only act tagged with it. Dropping it would empty the Budget filter on the roster page entirely, which costs a planner with the smallest spend the one act that actually answers them. It is honest as well: solo voice and guitar is the smallest live booking on this roster. If the Budget pill under a named artist's face reads wrong, it is one tag to delete.
_img_note: His own photograph, not an interim still: a black and white frame of him playing an acoustic guitar under string lights, cropped 16:9 from the centre of the source. Provenance in media-sources.json. It also releases standards.jpg, which the retired Blues Rock card shared with the jazz duo.
alt: Tony Medina playing an acoustic guitar under string lights, in black and white.
_video_note: SWAPPED 2026-09-06, Daniel's call, and this is a hosting decision as much as a taste one. The hero was t_s2FavrDew, the Freddie King duo cut, which sits on the SIDEHATCH ARTS channel rather than Tony's. That put the most-watched thing on the page on a channel we do not control: the views accrued to someone else, and a deletion or an embed switch on their side would have blanked the top of the page with no warning. It was also the weakest footage of the five once the frames were actually compared, at 720p in a plain office space with a second player as prominent as Tony. This is the Signet copy of his Prince cover instead: 1080p, purple stage light, unmistakably him out front, and we own it. Going Down keeps its place in the footage grid as the one duo performance.
blurb: Tony Medina has a smoky voice, and he plays guitar with all the rhythm of a funk player. He plays the blues and the rock and roll that came out of it, from Freddie King and B.B. King to The Cars and Prince, along with his own songs. He can play solo for welcome drinks and dinner, or bring a four piece when you want people dancing.
seo_title: Tony Medina: blues and rock for Denver private events
meta_description: Tony Medina plays blues and rock for private events in Denver and the Colorado mountains. You can book him solo or as a four piece. Just send us your date.
identity: Book Tony Medina when you want a singer who sounds like he's lived a little. He's a lot of fun to watch, too.
Your guests will likely know most of the covers.
We're happy to help you pick the right size for your event.

ladder.bestFor: On his own, he's an easy pick for welcome drinks, patios and dinner, and your guests shouldn't have to raise their voices.
A percussionist gives him a little more rhythm, and that's a nice touch at a patio event or a reception.
If your venue is on the small side, the trio can still get people dancing.

ladder.build: The trio plus a second guitar or keys
ladder.bestFor: This is his full dance band. We'd suggest it for office parties and milestone birthdays.

setlist._note: Every title here is a cover he publishes footage of, on this page or on his own channel, so the sample set and the evidence are the same list. Deliberately not from_repertoire: that branch picks the first N titles in catalogue order and would have printed the same songs as the Tejas Singh page.
setlist.note: Watch the video clips to see him play these covers. His full song list runs from sixties soul and classic rock through nineties alternative, and we'll put the setlist together around the flow of your event. This is just a sample, so the songs he plays at your event will be a little different.

_depth_note: Freddy Alexander was the other half of the interchangeable pair behind the retired Blues Rock format. He is not a listing and he is not published: `depth` renders on no surface, and this is the same unpublished availability depth he has been since 2026-08-16. The face-led promise above already covers him honestly, because it says any substitution is named to you in advance rather than pretending there is never one.
